question.text: What is the key difference between an Investor Service Center (ISC) operated by an AMC and an RTA service center like CAMS or KFintech?

answer.text: ISCs can process only purchase transactions while RTA centers handle only redemptions
ISCs charge a fee for transactions while RTA centers provide free services
ISCs typically handle transactions for only that particular AMC, while RTA service centers can process transactions for all AMCs serviced by that RTA
ISCs are located only in metro cities while RTA centers operate only in non-metro areas

explanation.text: The Logic: In Indian mutual-fund operations, an AMC-operated Investor Service Center typically handles transactions and investor service requests for only the schemes of that particular AMC. An RTA service center — such as a CAMS or KFintech branch — by contrast acts as a shared front-office for every AMC that has appointed that RTA, so a single visit can process transactions across all of those AMCs. Restricting ISCs to purchases and RTAs to redemptions is incorrect (both handle all transaction types); investors are not directly charged at either type of center for standard processing; and there is no metro-vs-non-metro geographic split between the two. The Trap: Option A fabricates a transaction-type restriction that does not exist — both ISCs and RTA centers can handle all types of transactions. Option B is wrong — neither charges investors directly for processing transactions. Option D creates a geographic distinction that does not exist — both operate in various cities. Note: The specific distinction that AMC-operated ISCs handle only that AMC while CAMS/KFintech centers process transactions for all AMCs serviced by that RTA is not stated on the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook pages checked (which note that RTA offices serve as ISCs and that AMCs may keep ISC activity in-house or outsource to an RTA); the framing above reflects general industry practice in Indian mutual-fund distribution rather than a workbook citation.
